svg.aria-label: A ticket's life as a strip, with its consequential decisions marked by class
svg.title: A ticket's life as a strip, with its consequential decisions marked by class
svg.text: A ticket's life: every session cycle on it, by role, and the decisions that changed what shipped or how
A cycle runs from one delivered turn (launch, wake, gate) to the next; dots are consequential decisions coded by reader A, coloured by what could have made them.
A median ticket: LIN-2803, 185 production lines, LinearViewer
41 session cycles over 1.8 h (1.8 h with a cycle running; quieter gaps over 45 min folded at the dashed lines). 7 consequential decisions: 1 a, 2 b, 4 c.

circle.title: S2.0 CE by research (frontier), class c: 'Ticket is partly stale': since LIN-1903/1904 drill-down is already provenance-aware, so the 'every single-provider surface reads the active binding only' claim is wrong; line citations shifted by LIN-2802.

S2.0 SC by research (frontier), class c: Record LIN-2819 as the reason Jira's new-workspace verb is provisional; plan then withheld Jira's newWorkspaceVerb ('mode=new still rejoins the existing container'), shipping the verb on GitHub only.
S3.0 SC by plan (mid), class c: Post-bind flash written at 4 add-source sites; 'the account-merge detour deliberately not wired — accepted degradation'.
S3.0 RT by plan (mid), class b: 'plan-review due: yes — sole trigger is the named contract gap (LIN-2819, routed around rather than fixed)'; plan-review then approved with non-blocking notes.

S1.9 CE by autopilot (frontier), class a: Worker posted done while its e2e run was in flight; autopilot found no commit, no pushed branch, no PR on the remote and sent a follow-up asking for e2e result, commit, push, PR and green CI.

S6.1 RT by review (frontier), class b: Approve-conditional: ledger item 4 (interface.js addProvider contract omits the two new facts) is inside scope and must be done before Done; handed to close-out, which landed it as ae9d7b62.

S7.1 MG by close-out (frontier), class c: Ledger item 1 (live bind to notice on GitHub/Jira/Linear) needed a real-credential repro or explicit accept; close-out established the harnesses are in-memory fakes, explicitly accepted it, and merged.

svg.text: A large ticket: LIN-2720, 301 production lines, simple-dispatcher
123 session cycles over 16.2 h (5.2 h with a cycle running; quieter gaps over 45 min folded at the dashed lines). 18 consequential decisions: 0 a, 3 b, 15 c.

circle.title: S1.3 CE by stepper (frontier), class c: Stepper noticed the live dispatcher at /Users/work/development/simple-dispatcher drives this session, 'so the primary log evidence is reachable rather than "on John's Mac, inaccessible" as the scope carve assumed'; it pointed beat 2 at the log.

S2.2 CE by research (frontier), class c: 'Answer: nothing killed it. It exited normally, by design' - the primary log refutes all four filed hypotheses and the BST timeline; the ticket 'asked for a right fix while describing the wrong cause'.

S3.5 SC by other-worker (frontier), class c: Design re-derived the sibling rulings rather than copying them: 'A ruling flipped on re-check - LIN-2377 FOLD->SEPARATE'. It was carried forward as LIN-2377 SEPARATE.

S3.5 ES by other-worker (frontier), class c: Design framed John's call: the acceptance criteria name killing the runner, which never reproduces the orderly-park bug; options costed, 'Recommendation: option 1'; 'amending the acceptance criteria is the author's call'.

S4.0 CE by plan (frontier), class c: Plan beat 1 tested the design's containment claim and found two containment gaps plus the pendingExternalRefireCount sizing gap; beat 2 resolved them into a widened guard and 'stamp the count, never refiredAt'.

S4.4 CE by plan (frontier), class c: Planning found 'element 7': the honest park routes every OpenCode wait through a stale-exit-sentinel race that would terminalize it COMPLETED with a false [done]. Seven elements, not six.
S5.1 SB by plan-review (frontier), class c: Plan-review Request Changes: F1 element 7 covers one EXECUTING-commit seam of three, F2 the new applies name no phase, F3 element 5's divert has no prompt.

S7.1 SB by plan-review (frontier), class c: Cycle-2 Request Changes: a consumer-side sweep finds findStalledOpenCodeLaunches force-fails every resume within ~5s; it recommends routing to John under the loop bound.

S1.35 ES by stepper (frontier), class c: 'Autopilot - pulling up: this is the second plan-review Request Changes, and the pattern is now the finding'. It parks rather than dispatch Revision 3, arguing every pass found a larger surface.

comment 09-10T20:48 SC by Runner (frontier), class b: Runner relaying to John: the opencode-runner.js:641 live defect 'already has a ticket', LIN-2652, so no new urgent ticket was filed. It also folded the acceptance-wording decision into the same ruling and framed four options.

comment 09-10T21:00 RU by John (human), class c: John: 'Worth a refactoring in advance.' Widen: the three-representations refactor becomes its own blocking ticket (LIN-2735) and LIN-2720 is re-planned on top. No third revision cycle.

comment 09-11T06:09 RU by John (human), class c: Acceptance-wording ruling: John says 'Adopt'. The three-clause wording (orderly park survives, runner death recovered, no stale-sentinel false [done]) becomes the acceptance criteria.

S9.4 RP by plan (frontier), class c: Revision 3 re-planned on LIN-2735's landed seam: 'Two of seven elements retire', with the resumedAt-stamp strategy chosen and a flagged deviation (no deferredAt in the activation max, contrary to N4).

S8.11 RT by stepper (frontier), class b: Override: recommend-and-dispatch pinned to implementation rather than the engine's breakdown, because plan section 11 says 'No Linear subtasks are minted - the split is the dispatch unit for the implement step'.

S11.0 SC by implementation (mid), class c: The plan's section 7 Clause 2 test/system/ scenario would need runOnce plumbing outside the session's scope, so implementation 'substituted equivalent coverage at the runStallFailsafe unit level' and flagged it for session 2.

S12.1 SB by review (frontier), class b: Approve was conditional, but 'F1 is the one item I would want fixed before merge regardless' (M6 survives: a vacuous effort-guard fixture). The ledger rows were carried into the C4 session, which fixed F1.

S15.1 SC by close-out (frontier), class c: Close-out gave each ledger row a disposition: it filed residue as LIN-2763, LIN-2764 and LIN-2765 and routed three rows to LIN-2751 with a scope-addition comment.

S15.1 MG by close-out (frontier), class c: Set Done with the four OpenCode e2e targets unavailable: 'Closed here with system-level coverage as the explicit accepted bound' rather than holding against the LIN-1474 environmental blocker.
